meta.title: Skipping Your 401k Match Is Turning Down Part of Your Paycheck
meta.hook: If your employer offers a 401k match and you're not claiming it, you're turning down part of your paycheck.
meta.description: A 401k match is extra compensation your employer adds only when you contribute to your own retirement account — it functions as an immediate, guaranteed addition to what you put in, separate from any investment returns. Skipping it means that portion of compensation is never paid at all. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: If your employer offers a 401k match and you're not claiming it, you're turning down part of your paycheck.

scenes.narration: A 401k match is extra money your employer adds, but only if you contribute first.

visual.visual_intent: A desk with retirement account paperwork and a pen, neutral light, still

scenes.narration: Say your employer matches fifty cents for every dollar you put in, up to six percent of your pay.

visual.visual_intent: Coins being matched in pairs on a dark surface, symbolic macro shot
visual.decision_reason: illustrative example structure, common real-world match format, framed as an example not a universal rate

overlays.text: Example: 50% match up to 6% of pay

scenes.narration: Contribute that six percent, and you instantly gain an extra three percent of your salary. Guaranteed, before any investment gains.

visual.visual_intent: A small coin stack with a sprouting plant growing from it, symbolic macro
visual.decision_reason: illustrates the immediate compensation gain from the example match rate

scenes.narration: No stock market return works like that. It's not a bet, it's compensation you have to actively claim.

visual.decision_reason: reframes the match as compensation, not a market bet

scenes.narration: Skip the match entirely, and that money simply never gets paid to you at all.

scenes.narration: It's the closest thing to free money in personal finance, and it's opt-in.
